claims.text: The starting HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The starting HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The starting HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a BCC matrix in the relevant initial state.
Aging HfZrTiTa0.53 at approximately 750–800 °C for an optimized duration will produce uniformly dispersed nanoscale secondary precipitates.
The aging treatment will create a dual-phase microstructure consisting of nanoscale precipitates embedded in a BCC matrix.
The nanoscale precipitates will impede dislocation glide.
Precipitate-mediated obstruction of dislocation motion will increase dynamic strain hardening.
Increased dynamic strain hardening will delay the initiation and propagation of adiabatic shear bands.
Delayed adiabatic shear banding will improve uniform deformation during high-strain-rate compression.
The aged alloy will have greater resistance to strain localization during high-strain-rate loading.
The aged alloy will exhibit increased dynamic yield strength relative to the baseline.
The aged alloy will exhibit increased dynamic compressive strength relative to the baseline.
The aged alloy will exhibit a higher fracture strain relative to the baseline.
The aged alloy will exhibit more controlled impact-induced energy release during dynamic deformation.
Excessive precipitate coarsening during over-aging may cause embrittlement.
The predicted improvements apply under largely adiabatic dynamic compression at strain rates of 1000–3000 s^-1.

contradictions.description: The predicted dynamic strengths are said to increase relative to a baseline defined by quasi-static values, whereas the falsification experiment appropriately compares aged and unaged specimens under dynamic loading. Thus, the stated reference baseline for the dynamic-strength prediction is inconsistent or ambiguous.
